prize_parts.citation: for discoveries establishing the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its bioactive form, which made incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for B010 to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not rest on the opening unanimity, and neither do I. The scientific case is a continuous chain from proglucagon-derived peptides through the identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form, human physiology of the incretin effect and appetite regulation, and receptor biology, to long-acting agonists whose benefit has been shown in large independent outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease. Maturity is not in question, and no second achievement on the shortlist is both as mature and as cleanly allocated within three names. A stand-alone prize also avoids dividing three laureates across two parts, which would force a thin split for B006 (two names) or an openly disputed one for B008. The citation should name the physiology and the bioactive peptide and state that this work made the therapies possible, so that it does not read as if the drugs were an afterthought.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the real weakness and round 1 did not resolve it. Priority between Mojsov and the Habener group for the bioactive peptide is unverified by any of us, Habener is not among the credited names on this ballot, and Knudsen is left out by the three-person cap, so the prize honours the discovery and not the medicinal chemistry that produced liraglutide and semaglutide. Some will read that as rewarding the less decisive step. Unanimity in an opening ballot also raises the risk that we settle the allocation too quickly. If a documentary check showed Mojsov's contribution to be derivative of the Habener work, the three-name configuration would fail even though the science is clearly worthy, and the ballot cannot supply the replacement name.

responses.point: Sandberg says a prize built on a contested allocation may age worse than a cleaner pairing such as B020, and that if B010 fails the fallback is unclear because B006 has no first-place support and an incomplete attribution.
responses.response: The fallback question is fair, and I do not claim B006 is a comfortable one. But I would not move to B020 to avoid a contested name: Walter and Mori have the tidiest attribution on the list, yet the medical relevance of the unfolded protein response is still mostly conceptual and disease-associated, not an established intervention. A clean pair is not a substitute for a larger and better-documented achievement. I keep your condition and have made it mine: if the primary record shows Mojsov's work to be derivative, I withdraw support for this three-name set and would then favour a two-name B006 over B020 as the fallback, with the Eshhar defect stated openly. I disagree that the allocation looks worse as it ages unless the priority check fails.

responses.point: Perlmann would not reduce B006 to two names before the Eshhar question is resolved, and he holds B010 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov while noting that excluding Knudsen honours the physiology and not the drugs.
responses.response: I accept your Eshhar condition as it applies to B006 in any form, and it is why I treat B006 only as a fallback and not as a second part beside B010. Where I would answer you on B010 is Knudsen. The cap forces a choice, and I choose the discoverers because the biological principle that justified long-acting agonists was established by the physiologists before the chemistry. I do not think that makes Knudsen's work incidental, and she remains first reserve if any of the three weakens. I also think the long-term obesity data you raise bear on how the drugs are used, not on whether the discovery was real, so I would not let them reduce the weight of the case. We still lack a primary-source check on Mojsov that none of us can do from the supplied record.

responses.point: Linnarsson, as summarised in round 1, treats the discovery-to-therapy arc as unusually complete, includes the drug development in that arc, and ranked B045 third in the opening round, though no round-1 list carries it as an alternative.
responses.response: I agree the arc is complete and I have kept the citation wording that says the discoveries made the therapies possible, which answers your concern about not treating the drugs as an afterthought. On B045 I have reconsidered. The mechanism-to-drug arc for SMN2 splicing is clear, but I still read it as early and at risk of being seen as recognition of antisense technology in general, and Krainer and Bennett do not settle the question of other contributors. I therefore do not move it into my alternatives, and I do not see it as a rival to B010 in this year. If you think the maturity argument is wrong, I would want to hear the specific evidence for durable long-term outcomes.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius asks why Deisseroth should be credited ahead of Boyden on B008, and says Sabatini's exclusion from B044 should be argued on credit allocation and not on personal standing, while also asking whether B010 should be paired with a second achievement.
responses.response: Your question about Deisseroth and Boyden is the one I cannot answer from the record, and that is why I now hold B008 as an alternative of lower standing than B006: the three-name allocation (Deisseroth, Nagel, Hegemann) leaves Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck with credible claims, and I know of no documented basis that ranks one trio ahead of the other. On pairing, my answer is that a second part would dilute a prize that already has a single well-defined achievement, unless the attribution question for the second part can be defended as well as B010 is defended. B008 cannot meet that standard now, and B006 cannot without Eshhar.

responses.point: El-Manira holds that the Prize has rewarded methods that opened intractable questions, so optogenetics should not be penalised for being a tool, and his citation for B010 speaks of establishing the incretin axis.
responses.response: I accept your historical point that methods have been honoured, and I do not rest my objection to B008 on the discovery-versus-tool distinction alone. My objection is that the clinical reach is still early and the allocation is disputed, so both maturity and exact credit are weaker than for B010. On your citation wording, I prefer the form that says the discoveries made the therapies possible, because establishing the incretin axis could be read as including Habener's group, and what we can actually defend is the physiology and the bioactive peptide. I am still open to your wording if the priority check leaves the Mojsov question as it is and you can say what the phrase excludes.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification of the bioactive GLP-1 peptide is separable from the Habener group's work. None of us has checked the primary papers and dates, and I treat that check as a precondition, not a formality.

If that check leaves her priority unsettled, whether the committee proceeds with this three-name set or needs a different name set that the supplied ballot cannot provide, since Habener is not among the credited names.
Whether Knudsen should be first reserve or whether the cap settles her exclusion, and whether the citation wording adequately signals that the drugs were not an afterthought.
Which fallback is best if B010 does not secure four votes: B006 with June and Sadelain, with Eshhar outside the credited names, or B008 with a disputed split.
Durability of weight-loss effects and long-term safety of the obesity indications, which I regard as separate from the case for the discovery.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. I have co-authored with Thomas Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1, autophagy), a collaboration between colleagues and not a connection to any shortlisted candidate or credited name. My postdoctoral work with Paul Greengard has no apparent link to any shortlisted candidate. I am not aware of any conflict requiring recusal on any shortlisted ballot.
